Bank stocks underperformed on the revival of risk that agentic AI erodes the customer inertia underpinning low-cost deposits, according to a research note by BofA Securities.

"The next phase of deposit disruption is not faster money movement, but reduced decision latency. Whereas a chatbot can tell customers they are earning too little, an agent can identify excess liquidity, compare yields, and act," said analysts Ebrahim Poonawala, Brandon Berman, Gabriel Angelini, and Michael Campos.
was down 3.42% to $340.00, Bank of America

"For banks, the proof point is not downloads, daily-active-users or app-store rankings. The metric that matters is deposit betas, in our view. If agentic AI is genuinely changing behavior, evidence should emerge through higher deposit costs, lower non-interest-bearing balances, and greater competition for marginal funding," said BofA.

"Until deposit costs rise faster than can be explained by rates or competition, the disruption thesis remains conceptual. App adoption establishes the opportunity; deposit betas will establish the disruption," said the note.
